questions.explanation: The job is cancelled while it is suspended in `delay`, so `delay` throws `CancellationException` and the `finally` block runs. `cancelAndJoin()` waits for the job to finish, `finally` included, so "cleanup" is printed before "done".

questions.question: What does it mean that coroutine cancellation is cooperative?
options: `cancel()` only marks the job; the coroutine stops when its code next checks for cancellation
`cancel()` interrupts the thread running the coroutine, the same way `Thread.interrupt()` does
`cancel()` stops the coroutine at whatever instruction it is running, wherever that is
A coroutine can only be cancelled if it was launched with a `SupervisorJob`
questions.explanation: Cancelling sets the job's state to cancelling. Nothing stops until the coroutine reaches a check (`delay`, `yield`, `ensureActive()`, `isActive`, ...). The thread is not interrupted, and the code is never killed partway through.

questions.question: If a coroutine is cancelled while it is suspended in `delay(5_000)`, `delay` resumes right away by throwing a `CancellationException`, without waiting out the 5 seconds.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: All suspending functions in kotlinx.coroutines are cancellable. `delay` is woken up at once and throws `CancellationException`, which unwinds the coroutine through its `finally` blocks.

questions.question: A `viewModelScope.launch { repo.sync() }` is suspended in a network call when the user leaves the screen and the ViewModel is cleared. What happens?
options: The coroutine gets a `CancellationException` at its suspension point and stops
The coroutine keeps running until `sync()` returns, and only then is the scope cancelled
The app crashes because the coroutine outlived its ViewModel
The coroutine is paused and resumes if the user comes back to the screen
questions.explanation: When the ViewModel is cleared, `viewModelScope` is cancelled, which cancels every coroutine in it. A cancellable suspend call (such as a Retrofit `suspend` function) throws `CancellationException`, and the work stops quietly. Nothing crashes, and nothing is paused to resume later.

questions.question: A coroutine runs a long CPU-bound loop with no suspension points, so `cancel()` doesn't stop it. Which changes make the loop respond to cancellation? Select all that apply.
options: Check `isActive` in the loop condition
Call `ensureActive()` on each iteration
Call `yield()` on each iteration
Call `Thread.sleep(1)` on each iteration
Wrap the loop body in `try { } catch (e: Exception) { }`
questions.explanation: `isActive` lets you exit the loop yourself, `ensureActive()` throws `CancellationException` if the job is cancelled, and `yield()` checks for cancellation and also lets other coroutines run. `Thread.sleep` is a blocking JVM call that knows nothing about the job, and a broad `catch` only makes cancellation easier to swallow.

The job stays cancelled, so iteration 2's `delay` throws at once and is caught as well. After that, "loop end" still runs. Rethrow `CancellationException`, or catch only specific exceptions.

questions.question: What is the difference between `job.cancel()` and `job.cancelAndJoin()`?
options: `cancel()` returns at once; `cancelAndJoin()` also waits until the job has fully finished
`cancel()` is cooperative, while `cancelAndJoin()` force-stops the job even inside a CPU loop
`cancelAndJoin()` cancels the job and every other coroutine in the same scope
There is no difference. `cancelAndJoin()` is a deprecated alias
questions.explanation: `cancel()` is a non-suspending request, so the job may still be running its cleanup when the call returns. `cancelAndJoin()` is `cancel()` followed by `join()`. It doesn't force anything either: a non-cooperative job still runs to completion, and `cancelAndJoin()` just waits for it.

questions.question: Calling `job.cancel()` interrupts a `Thread.sleep(5_000)` that is running inside the coroutine, so the job stops immediately.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Cancellation doesn't interrupt threads. `Thread.sleep` blocks the thread for the full 5 seconds and the coroutine only notices the cancellation at its next check. Use `delay` instead, or `runInterruptible` to wrap blocking code that should be interrupted.

questions.question: After cancellation, this job prints "closing" but never "closed". Why, and what is the usual fix?
options: The cancelled job makes `delay` in `finally` throw. Wrap it in `withContext(NonCancellable)`
`finally` blocks don't run on cancellation. Move the cleanup into a `catch (e: CancellationException)` block
`println` can't be called after cancellation. Use a logger instead
The `delay` is skipped because `finally` code runs on a different thread. Replace it with `Thread.sleep(100)`
questions.explanation: `finally` does run, but the job is cancelled, so any cancellable suspend call in it throws straight away. `withContext(NonCancellable)` runs the cleanup in a context that ignores the cancellation, so suspending calls there complete normally.

questions.explanation: A scope whose `Job` is cancelled can't run new work. `launch` doesn't throw: it returns a child that is cancelled straight away, so the block never runs. This is why a cancelled `viewModelScope` silently ignores new `launch` calls.

questions.question: This polling loop runs in a ViewModel. What happens after the user leaves the screen and `viewModelScope` is cancelled?
options: It never ends: `runCatching` swallows each `CancellationException` and the loop spins
The loop stops at the next `delay` because `viewModelScope` was cancelled
The app crashes with an uncaught `CancellationException`
`runCatching` rethrows `CancellationException` automatically, so the coroutine ends cleanly
questions.explanation: `runCatching` catches every `Throwable`, `CancellationException` included. `while (true)` never checks `isActive`, so the cancelled coroutine keeps calling suspend functions that fail at once, and it never finishes. Use `while (isActive)`, or rethrow `CancellationException` from the failure branch.

questions.question: Which statements about `withTimeout` and `withTimeoutOrNull` are true? Select all that apply.
options: `withTimeout` throws `TimeoutCancellationException` when the time runs out
`TimeoutCancellationException` is a subclass of `CancellationException`
If the block can itself return `null`, a `null` from `withTimeoutOrNull` doesn't tell you whether it timed out
When the timeout fires, the block keeps running in the background and only its result is thrown away
`TimeoutCancellationException` can't be caught with try/catch because it is a `CancellationException`
questions.explanation: On timeout the block is cancelled (cooperatively, like any cancellation) and `withTimeout` throws `TimeoutCancellationException`, a `CancellationException` subclass that you can catch like any other exception. `withTimeoutOrNull` uses `null` to mean a timeout, which is ambiguous when the block can also return `null`.

questions.question: This wraps a location callback. What happens if the calling coroutine is cancelled while it waits for a fix?
options: The caller gets `CancellationException` at once, and the handler unregisters the callback
The caller keeps waiting until the next location arrives, then throws
The callback is removed automatically even without `invokeOnCancellation`
Nothing happens. A coroutine suspended in `suspendCancellableCoroutine` can't be cancelled
questions.explanation: `suspendCancellableCoroutine` makes the suspension point cancellable: on cancel, the caller is resumed with `CancellationException` at once, and the `invokeOnCancellation` handler runs. The coroutine library can't know how to unregister your listener, so without the handler the callback and anything it references would leak.

questions.question: If a `Deferred` from `async` is cancelled before it finishes, calling `await()` on it throws a `CancellationException` instead of returning a value.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A cancelled `Deferred` has no result, so `await()` throws `CancellationException`. Like `delay` and `withContext`, `await` also throws if the coroutine calling it is cancelled while it waits.

questions.question: The user leaves the screen while this transaction is suspended in `api.fetchItems()`, and `viewModelScope` is cancelled. What happens to the database?
options: The transaction rolls back, so neither the delete nor the insert is committed
The delete is committed and the insert is lost, leaving the table empty
Room ignores cancellation inside `withTransaction`, so both statements always commit
The database is left locked until the app restarts
questions.explanation: `withTransaction` commits only if the block completes normally. Here `api.fetchItems()` throws `CancellationException`, which escapes the block and ends the transaction without marking it successful, so SQLite rolls back the delete too. (Holding a transaction open across a network call is a bad idea anyway: fetch first, then write.) If the write must finish even after the user leaves, run it in an application-level scope or wrap it in `withContext(NonCancellable)`.

questions.question: You wrap an OkHttp `Call` with `suspendCancellableCoroutine`, calling `enqueue` and resuming from `onResponse`/`onFailure`. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: If the coroutine is cancelled, the caller gets `CancellationException` right away without waiting for OkHttp's callback
The HTTP request keeps running unless you call `call.cancel()` from `invokeOnCancellation`
Calling `cont.resume(response)` after the coroutine was cancelled crashes with `IllegalStateException`
Using `suspendCoroutine` instead would cancel the request automatically
The `invokeOnCancellation` handler also runs when the call succeeds and resumes normally
questions.explanation: The continuation is cancellable, so the caller isn't kept waiting, but OkHttp knows nothing about coroutines and only stops the request if you call `call.cancel()` in `invokeOnCancellation`. A plain `resume` on an already cancelled continuation is ignored (it doesn't crash), `suspendCoroutine` can't be cancelled at all, and the handler only runs on cancellation.

questions.question: Right after `job.cancel()` returns, before the job has finished its `NonCancellable` cleanup, what does the `println` print?
options: false true false
false true true
true true false
false false false
questions.explanation: After `cancel()` the job is in the Cancelling state: no longer active, `isCancelled` is true, but it hasn't completed because its `finally` block is still running. It becomes Cancelled (`isCompleted == true`) only when the cleanup finishes.
